rationale: The new VisitCase block is not gated on relational-nulls mode, so the emitted SQL changes there too, and the test base does have a CreateContext(useRelationalNulls: true) convention (e.g. line 779) that none of the five new tests use. Small, and many neighboring tests skip that variant too.

DropNotNullChecks only deletes matched IS NOT NULL conjuncts and rebuilds the AndAlso chain from the survivors; removing a conjunct cannot render a sibling conjunct trivially true or false, so the premise of the missed simplification does not hold.

func.InstancePropagatesNullability == true is the one constant comparison in the new code written with == rather than an is pattern, which is the same style preference the thread states ('I use is for any constant/literal check at this point'), applied to the surviving occurrence at the checkpoint.

The documented meaning of ArgumentsPropagateNullability/InstancePropagatesNullability is exactly 'this operand propagates null to the result', which is the implication the optimization relies on; the note identifies no contract change and asserts no defect.

_with_partial_checks checks A and B while the result also uses C (partial null checks) and _with_mixed_checks combines a null check with a non-null-check boolean (BoolA); both names match what they assert, so the claim that they are swapped is wrong.

The block is guarded by testIsCondition, which is defined as caseExpression.Operand == null, so no simple-CASE operand can be discarded; the cluster itself concedes the block is unreachable for one and asserts no defect.
SqlUnaryExpression's allowed operators are Equal, NotEqual, Convert, Not, Negate, and unary NotEqual is by construction IS NOT NULL, so the over-match concern is cleared with no defect asserted.

All five new tests have results built only from ~, arithmetic and string concatenation (totally null-propagating), so none exercises a boolean/comparison result where NullPropagatedOperands' unfiltered binary recursion (line 626) makes the drop unsound; a real gap no thread raises.

Membership is structural equality over SqlExpression, so two separate evaluations of the same non-deterministic nullable expression are treated as one; the soundness argument ('operand null implies result null') then does not hold. Real but exotic.

The partial-checks test does reach the false arm via COALESCE (argumentsPropagateNullability [false,false]), but its assertion would not change if the flag check were inverted, so no test pins the soundness-critical branch. Small but correct.

Correct — [MemberNotNullWhen(false, nameof(Arguments), nameof(ArgumentsPropagateNullability))] is what makes the guard load-bearing — but it is a considered-and-cleared note defending existing code and asserts no defect.

Matching only unary NotEqual can at worst forgo the optimization, never make it unsound, and the factory normalizes Not(IS NULL) to unary NotEqual; the note raises a missed-optimization possibility without establishing one.

Half wrong: the Convert path is exercised by the updated baselines (CASE ... CAST(LEN(x) AS int) collapses to CAST(LEN(x) AS int) in Null_propagation_optimization5/6). Only Negate is untested, and an untested unary arm of a best-effort optimizer is not reviewer-worthy.
IsNull's parameter arm is deliberate and safe — the comment directly above it states the query is cached by parameter nullability — so a parameter-value-dependent rewrite is by design, not a defect.

The unfiltered 'else if (expression is SqlBinaryExpression binary)' recursion marks operands of AndAlso/OrElse as null-propagating, which is false in SQL (FALSE AND NULL = FALSE), so DropNotNullChecks can remove an IS NOT NULL and turn a NULL result into FALSE — the same defect the thread raises about non-null-propagating binary operators being treated as propagating.
Both helpers dispatch through if/else-if type-pattern chains; the thread asks for exactly this to be folded into one switch with pattern matching.

Same substance as the thread's 'AtTimeZone, Collate' remark: NullPropagatedOperands enumerates a closed set of node types and omits other node types that do propagate null (LikeExpression among them). Different instance, same omission; hence the reduced confidence.
The cluster states outright that the rendering is pre-existing and unchanged by this diff, so it asserts no defect in the change under review.

Unbounded recursion over expression trees is the prevailing pattern throughout SqlNullabilityProcessor and the wider visitor infrastructure; flagging it here without a depth argument specific to this code is not actionable.

The SqlFunctionExpression constructor throws InconsistentNumberOfArguments unless Arguments.Count equals ArgumentsPropagateNullability.Count, so the flag list cannot be longer; the same loop shape is already used at lines 2399-2405.
